clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and your mother's anxiety rose as she lay awake over her mother and Anton; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work; your brother Callum's ear infections came one after another all winter. By May 1979, your grandmother had taken a job at the library and was out of the house every day, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Odette's pregnancy, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother being ordered to bed for the rest of her pregnancy in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house and argued with your father over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. These shifts are enough because they cluster within three months of a clear change in your mother's functioning, and no one else's shifts show in those months.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis with Parkinson's disease in September 1986, within the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments and later hardly left her side as her functioning fell; your father phoned his father every night for news and later argued with Uncle Lyle over who should help their parents, then fought with your mother over his evenings at their house; your aunt Pearl's panic spells began at the wheel and she stopped driving on the motorway; your Uncle Anton drank most evenings. By June 1997, when your grandmother moved into the nursing home, the shifts settled around her new place.

clusters.name: Callum leaving for the mines, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home in May 1999 for a job up north: your father and he argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn. By August 2000, when your sister was back at school full days and passed her exams, the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night, stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May, and dreaded buses and crowded shops, going out only after dark. By November 2003, when you took a job at the garden centre and were sleeping through the night again, the shifts settled. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
